summary: Bonner County, ID lookout: c.1934 40-ft pole tower with L-4 cab; unused after 1950; 1962 report of towers being toppled and burned; now gone or removed.

facts.status_note: Idaho Fire Lookouts and firelookout.com say gone; Forest Lookouts gives its status as Removed; a June 1962 Sandpoint News Bulletin report, quoted by Forest Lookouts, says the lookouts were being toppled and destroyed

staffing.status: no documented staffing history on Idaho Fire Lookouts

visit.trail_note: Idaho Fire Lookouts tags the site Hike-In; no source describes what remains there now

events.note: 40-foot pole tower with L-4 cab; dated c.1934 by Forest Lookouts (Kresek) and 1934 by firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts
Not used or maintained since 1950, when the Forest Service went to aerial patrol (per June 1962 Sandpoint News Bulletin report)

June 1962 Sandpoint News Bulletin report lists Strawberry Mountain among six abandoned lookouts in the process of being toppled and destroyed; towers reported being burned. No later source confirms the outcome.

notes_for_editor: Name is shared with other Strawberry Mountain lookouts in search results (Washington state; a working tower near McCall, Idaho). This record covers only the Bonner County site. Brief's height 12.2 m matches the 40-ft pole tower. Fate rests on a 1962 newspaper report that towers were being toppled and burned; no later source confirms the outcome, and Forest Lookouts gives status Removed. Idaho Fire Lookouts gives no staffing history, so staffing is omitted from the story. No site condition found today. Hike-In tag read as drive_up false.
